title: Multi-Stage Flash Vessel
model_title: Multi-Stage Flash Train (Blow-Off / Flash Tanks after Digestion)

introduction.definition: A multi-stage flash train lowers the pressure of hot digested slurry in steps. In each tank some water flashes to steam and the slurry cools; that vapour is used to heat incoming slurry, recovering heat.
introduction.summary: After digestion the hot slurry passes through a train of flash tanks at falling pressure. In each tank part of the water flashes to steam, cooling the slurry; the vapour heats incoming slurry in the matching heaters.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Temperature profile falls stage by stage; heat recovered ∝ flash steam.

pressure.title: Stepwise pressure reduction recovers heat
pressure.description: Hot digested slurry is let down in steps to lower pressures; in each tank part of the water flashes to steam and the slurry cools to the saturation temperature of that stage. The flash vapour from each stage heats incoming slurry in the matching heater stage (regenerative heating). Erosion at let-down valves and inlets is a key concern.

foundation: Supports designed for operating, test and wind/seismic loads; allow thermal expansion.
alignment: Vertical vessels plumb; let-down valves and lines supported against vibration.
piping: Relief protection per code; erosion-resistant fittings at let-down points; steam traps/condensate removal; insulation.
commissioning: Hydro-test; heat up slowly; check relief settings, levels, temperatures and pressures; test interlocks.

video_tutorials.title: Multi-Stage Flash Vessel — Operation

script.narration: How the Multi-Stage Flash Vessel works.
Digested slurry enters tank 1 at high pressure.
Part of the water flashes to steam.
Vapour goes to the matching heater.
Slurry passes to the next lower-pressure tank.
The last tank discharges at near-atmospheric pressure.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Hot digested slurry is let down in steps to lower pressures; in each tank part of the water flashes to steam and the slurry cools to the saturation temperature of that stage.

video_tutorials.title: Multi-Stage Flash Vessel — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Multi-Stage Flash Vessel.
Check levels and let-down valves.
Thickness checks; wear liners.
Valve trim replacement.
Watch for erosion: leaks, thinning. Common cause: two-phase high velocity.
Watch for carry-over: slurry in vapour lines. Common cause: high level.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
